resource.name: aws_cloudwatch_log_resource_policy
resource.description: Provides a resource to manage a CloudWatch log resource policy.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_cloudwatch_log_resource_policy` Terraform resource enables the creation and management of IAM resource policies for CloudWatch Logs, allowing users to define access permissions for log groups across AWS accounts or services. Common use cases include granting cross-account access to log data, integrating CloudWatch Logs with AWS services like Lambda or Kinesis, and enforcing fine-grained security controls for log management. This resource supports configurations for policy statements, permissions, and access scopes, making it essential for secure and scalable log monitoring setups.

examples.title: Elasticsearch Log Publishing
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an `aws_cloudwatch_log_resource_policy` to enable Elasticsearch to publish logs to CloudWatch Logs. It showcases the use of an `aws_iam_policy_document` data source to define permissions for the `es.amazonaws.com` service, including actions like `CreateLogStream` and `PutLogEvents`, and applies the policy using the `policy_document` and `policy_name` arguments.

examples.title: Route53 Query Logging
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an `aws_cloudwatch_log_resource_policy` to enable Route53 query logging by defining an IAM policy document that grants Route53 service permissions to create log streams and put log events in CloudWatch Logs. It showcases the use of the `policy_document` argument to reference a dynamically generated policy and highlights the integration of service principals and resource-specific permissions.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument for the `aws_cloudwatch_log_resource_policy` resource represents the unique identifier of the resource policy, typically auto-generated by AWS upon creation. While optional, it can be used to reference or manage the policy programmatically, aiding in resource tracking and integration with other infrastructure components.

arguments.name: policy_document
arguments.description: (Required) Details of the resource policy, including the identity of the principal that is enabled to put logs to this account. This is formatted as a JSON string. Maximum length of 5120 characters.
arguments.llm_summary: The `policy_document` argument in the `aws_cloudwatch_log_resource_policy` resource allows users to define the JSON-formatted resource policy that specifies which principals (e.g., AWS services, accounts, or roles) are authorized to send log events to the account. By configuring this argument, users enable controlled access to CloudWatch Logs, ensuring secure and compliant log ingestion from specified sources.

arguments.name: policy_name
arguments.llm_summary: The `policy_name` argument specifies the unique name of the CloudWatch Logs resource policy, allowing users to define and identify the policy that governs permissions for log groups. Setting this argument ensures the policy can be referenced and managed, enabling control over access and security configurations for log data.
